heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li II.i.19 … Qu Li II.ii.4
Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li (opening) … Qu Li I.ii.2

items.text: In winter warm your parents' bed and cool it in summer; in the evening adjust everything for their repose, and ask about their health in the morning.
items.quote: In winter, to warm the bed for their parents, and to cool it in summer; ... to inquire about their health in the morning.

items.text: When you go to take counsel with an elder, carry a stool and staff for him; when he asks a question, do not answer without acknowledging your incompetency and declining.
items.quote: In going to take counsel with an elder, one must carry a stool and a staff with him (for the elder's use).

items.text: Attend your husband when he travels on service.
items.quote: When travelling on service, he must have the attendance of his wife

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li I.iv.14 … Qu Li I.v.4

items.text: Serve as the personator of your deceased grandfather at sacrifices.
items.quote: A grandson may be the personator of his deceased grandfather (at sacrifices), but a son cannot be so of his father.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration; consulting the dead is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: In mourning for your father, do not emaciate yourself or disable your senses; if you make yourself unable to perform the mourning duties, you are unkind and unfilial.
items.quote: If he make himself unable to perform his mourning duties, that is like being unkind and unfilial.

items.text: In mourning for your father, do not go up or down by the east steps he used, nor go in or out by the path opposite the gate.
items.quote: He should not go up to, nor descend from, the hall by the steps on the east (which his father used).

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li I.ii.3 … Qu Li I.iii.5

items.text: Honor your father's intimate friends: do not approach, retire, or address them unless bidden or questioned.
items.quote: When he sees an intimate friend of his father, not to presume to go forward to him without being told to do so.

items.text: When you go abroad, tell your parents where you are going; when you return, present yourself to them.
items.quote: A son, when he is going abroad, must inform (his parents where he is going); when he returns, he must present himself before them.

items.text: Do not use the term "old" for your parents in ordinary conversation.
items.quote: In ordinary conversation (with his parents), he does not use the term 'old' (with reference to them).

items.text: Do not occupy the south-west corner of the apartment, sit in the middle of the mat, walk in the middle of the road, or stand in the middle of the doorway.
items.quote: A son should not occupy the south-west corner of the apartment, nor sit in the middle of the mat, nor walk in the middle of the road.

items.text: Do not take the part of regulating the rice and other viands at an entertainment.
items.quote: He should not take the part of regulating the (quantity of) rice and other viands at an entertainment.

items.text: Do not act as personator of the dead at sacrifice.
items.quote: He should not act as personator of the dead at sacrifice.
items.conflict: Ancestral rites offered to the dead conflict with the exclusive worship of God and the prohibition of necromancy.

items.text: Be as if hearing your parents when they are silent and seeing them when they are absent.
items.quote: He should be (as if he were) hearing (his parents) when there is no voice from them, and as seeing them when they are not actually there.

items.text: Do not ascend heights, approach depths, revile or laugh recklessly, or attempt hazardous or secret things, lest you disgrace your parents.
items.quote: A filial son will not do things in the dark, nor attempt hazardous undertakings, fearing lest he disgrace his parents.

items.text: While your parents are alive, do not promise a friend to die with him, and do not have wealth that you call your own.
items.quote: While his parents are alive, he will not promise a friend to die (with or for him), nor will he have wealth that he calls his own.

items.text: Never allow a boy to see an instance of deceit.
items.quote: A boy should never be allowed to see an instance of deceit.

items.text: Serve one twice your age as you serve your father, one ten years older as an elder brother; walk a little behind one five years older.
items.quote: He should serve one twice as old as himself as he serves his father, one ten years older than himself as an elder brother.

items.text: When an elder holds your hand, hold his with both hands.
items.quote: When an elder is holding him with the hand, he should hold the elder's hand with both his hands.

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li I.v.5 … Qu Li I.v.42

items.text: Do not live under the same heaven with the enemy who has slain your father.
items.quote: With the enemy who has slain his father, one should not live under the same heaven.
items.conflict: Personal vengeance; Scripture says, 'Vengeance is mine, I will repay' (Rom 12:19).

items.text: Never let your sword rest until you avenge your slain brother.
items.quote: With the enemy who has slain his brother, one should never have his sword to seek (to deal vengeance).
items.conflict: Personal vengeance; Scripture says, 'Vengeance is mine, I will repay' (Rom 12:19).

items.text: After the wailing is over, do not speak of your deceased father by his name.
items.quote: When the ceremony of wailing is over, a son should no longer speak of his deceased father by his name.

items.text: While your parents live, do not utter your grandparents' names.
items.quote: While his parents (are alive), and a son is able to serve them, he should not utter the names of his grandparents.

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li I.iii.47 … Qu Li I.iv.13

items.text: If an elder personally hands you food, bow to him and eat it; if he does not hand it to you, eat without bowing.
items.quote: If the host give anything to him with his own hand, he should bow to him and eat it.

items.text: When drinking with an elder, rise, bow, and receive the cup at the wine-jar; do not drink until he has emptied his cup.
items.quote: When the cup of spirits is brought to him, he rises, bows... until he has emptied it, the other does not presume to drink his.

items.text: When an elder offers a gift, do not presume to decline it.
items.quote: When an elder offers a gift, neither a youth, nor one of mean condition, presumes to decline it.

items.text: When an elder calls you to share a feast, do not decline the food even if it is more than enough.
items.quote: Though the viands may be double (what is necessary), he should not (seek) to decline them.

items.text: When your father or mother is ill, deny yourself: do not comb your hair, walk with elbows out, talk idly, play the lute, eat rich food, drink, laugh broadly, or give way to anger until they recover.
items.quote: When his father or mother is ill... He should not eat of different meats till his taste is changed, nor drink till his looks are changed.

items.text: Do not use the ruler's leftover portions as an offering to a deceased son.
items.quote: A father should not use them in offering even to a (deceased) son.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with Deut. 18:10-12.

items.text: Do not use the ruler's leftover portions as an offering to a deceased wife.
items.quote: Nor a husband in offering to a (deceased) wife.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with Deut. 18:10-12.

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li I.v.43 … Qu Li II.i.18

items.text: Before your parent's burial study the mourning rites; after the burial study the sacrificial rites; after mourning ends resume ordinary life and music.
items.quote: before the interment of (a parent), (a son) should study the ceremonies of mourning, and after the interment, those of sacrifice.

items.text: Do not presume to call yourself 'little son' or 'inheriting son' as if you already stood in your father's place.
items.quote: The son of a Great officer ... should not presume to speak of himself as 'I, the little son.'

items.text: If you are left fatherless, do not change your name; if you later become noble, do not bestow an honorary title on your dead father.
items.quote: when left an orphan, will not change his name. Nor... frame an honorary title for his father.

items.text: When living in another state, keep your former state's sacrificial, mourning, and wailing customs exactly.
items.quote: His ceremonies in sacrifice, his dress during the period of mourning, and his positions in the wailing and weeping, will all be according to the fashions of his former (state).

items.text: If your branch still holds its hereditary dignity and kin remain in the old state, keep sending word of yourself to your ancestor's representative.
items.quote: he should (continue to) send back word about himself to the representative of his ancestor.

items.text: When building, give the ancestral temple first attention, then stables and arsenal, and only then residences.
items.quote: the ancestral temple should have his first attention, the stables and arsenal the next, and the residences the last.

items.text: As head of the clan, give first place to sacrificial vessels, then to sacrificial victims, and put meal vessels last.
items.quote: the vessels of sacrifice should have the first place; the victims supplied from his revenue, the next; and the vessels for use at meals, the last.

items.text: Do not sell sacrificial vessels, do not wear sacrificial robes for warmth, and do not cut down trees on grave-mounds.
items.quote: will not sell his vessels of sacrifice; though suffering from cold, he will not wear his sacrificial robes; ... will not cut down the trees on his grave-mounds.

items.text: During mourning do not speak of music; during sacrifice do not speak of inauspicious things.
items.quote: When occupied with the duties of mourning, one should not speak of music. When sacrificing, one should not speak of what is inauspicious.

items.text: Do not call your principal concubine by name.
items.quote: nor his principal concubine.
items.conflict: Concubinage/polygamy; marriage is one man and one woman (Gen 2:24; Matt 19:5).

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li II.iii.20

items.text: Be among those who provide sons for him.
items.quote: This is to complete the providers of sons for you.
items.conflict: Concubinage/polygamy conflicts with the creation ordinance of one man and one woman (Gen 2:24; Matt 19:4-6).

items.text: Be among those who provide his spirits and sauces.
items.quote: This is to complete the providers of your spirits and sauces.
items.conflict: Concubinage/polygamy conflicts with the creation ordinance of one man and one woman (Gen 2:24; Matt 19:4-6).

items.text: Be among those who sprinkle and sweep for him.
items.quote: This is to complete the number of those who sprinkle and sweep for you.
items.conflict: Concubinage/polygamy conflicts with the creation ordinance of one man and one woman (Gen 2:24; Matt 19:4-6).

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li II.ii.5 … Qu Li II.iii.3

items.text: Call yourself by your own name before your parents.
items.quote: To their parents, sons and daughters called themselves by their names.

items.text: If you have remonstrated three times and your parents still do not listen, follow your remonstrance with loud crying and tears.
items.quote: In the service of his parents by a son, if he have thrice remonstrated and is still not listened to, he should follow (his remonstrance) with loud crying and tears.

items.text: When your parent is ill, taste the medicine before giving it, and do not use a doctor whose family has not practiced medicine for three generations.
items.quote: The same is the rule for a son and an ailing parent.

items.text: Before your own lord, call yourself the small maid.
items.quote: To her own ruler she called herself 'the small maid.'

items.text: Call yourself your handmaid.
items.quote: From the honourable women downwards (each member of the harem) called herself 'your handmaid.'
items.conflict: Concubinage/polygamy; Scripture: one-flesh union of one man and one woman (Gen 2:24; Matt 19:5).

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li I.iii.6 … Qu Li I.iii.46

items.text: When your father calls, do not merely answer 'yes'; answer respectfully and rise at once.
items.quote: When his father calls, (a youth) should not (merely) answer 'yes,' nor when his teacher calls. He should, with (a respectful) 'yes,' immediately rise (and go to them).

items.text: Do not exchange personal inquiries between sister-in-law and brother-in-law.
items.quote: A sister-in-law and brother-in-law do not interchange inquiries (about each other).

items.text: When your married sister returns home, do not sit with her on the same mat or eat from the same dish.
items.quote: no brother (of the family) should sit with her on the same mat or eat with her from the same dish.

items.text: Do not share a mat with your daughter.
items.quote: (Even) the father and daughter should not occupy the same mat.

items.text: Do not have a concubine wash a son's lower garment.
items.quote: None of the concubines in a house should be employed to wash the lower garment (of a son).

items.text: Announce the day and month of your marriage to the ancestral spirits with purification and fasting.
items.quote: the day and month (of the marriage) should be announced to the ruler, and to the spirits (of ancestors) with purification and fasting
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is not worship of God alone (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Do not marry a wife of your own surname.
items.quote: One must not marry a wife of the same surname with himself.

items.text: If you buy a concubine and do not know her surname, consult the tortoise-shell.
items.quote: in buying a concubine, if he do not know her surname, he must consult the tortoise-shell about it.

items.text: Do not give a son a name that is a state, a day or month, a hidden ailment, or a hill or river.
items.quote: it should not be that of a state, nor of a day or a month, nor of any hidden ailment, nor of a hill or river.

items.text: Distinguish the ages of your sons and daughters.
items.quote: Sons and daughters should have their (relative) ages distinguished.

items.text: At twenty, cap your son and give him his appellation; when your daughter is promised in marriage, give her the hair-pin and her appellation.
items.quote: A son at twenty is capped, and receives his appellation. When a daughter is promised in marriage, she assumes the hair-pin, and receives her appellation.

items.text: Before your father, allow yourself to be called by your personal name, not by your appellation.
items.quote: Before his father a son should be called by his name, and before his ruler a minister.

heading: Liji 1 · Qu Li 曲禮 · Khü Lî · Qu Li II.iii.4 … Qu Li II.iii.19

items.text: Offer the five sacrifices of the house in the course of the year, as your station requires.
items.quote: Great officers present the oblations of the five sacrifices of the house,--all in the course of the year.
items.conflict: Ancestor sacrifice conflicts with Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20.

items.text: If you are an ordinary officer, present oblations to your ancestors.
items.quote: (Other) officers present oblations to their ancestors.
items.conflict: Ancestor sacrifice conflicts with Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20.

items.text: If you are the son of an inferior member of the harem and must offer the ancestral sacrifice, report it first to the honored son, the head of the family.
items.quote: The son of an inferior member of the harem cannot offer the sacrifice ... he must report it to the honoured son, (the head of the family).
items.conflict: Concubinage / inferior harem conflicts with Genesis 2:24; Hebrews 13:4.
items.needs_role: son of an inferior member of the harem

items.text: Do not abolish established sacrifices or resume abolished ones, and do not offer an improper sacrifice; a licentious sacrifice brings no blessing.
items.quote: There should be no presuming to resume any sacrifice which has been abolished ... nor to abolish any which has been so established. A licentious sacrifice brings no blessing.
items.conflict: Ancestor sacrifice conflicts with Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20.

items.text: In sacrificing, call your departed grandfather, grandmother, father, mother, and husband by their proper honorific titles.
items.quote: a grandfather is called 'the sovereign grandfather;' a grandmother, 'the sovereign grandmother;' a father, 'the sovereign father;' a mother, 'the sovereign mother; a husband, 'the sovereign pattern.'
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20.

items.text: After your father, mother, or wife dies, do not use their living names; use the proper posthumous title.
items.quote: when they are dead, those of 'the completed one (khâo),' 'the corresponding one (pî),' and 'the honoured one (pin).'
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20.
